author: cmungall
body: https://www.uniprot.org/arba/ARBA00086692 This rule is a disjunction of two conditions - one is scoped to Glires (which are within mammals) and fabids (which are within plants) However, the rule has been applied to a pseudomonas (a kind of bacteria) https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/annotations?geneProductId=Q88KS6 Note that the prediction does NOT show up on the uniprot page https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q88KS6/entry This leads me to think this is some kind of versioning/sync issue. Maybe the rule was more inclusive and has since become more restrictive, and it will drop out of QuickGO in time? If so, this makes determining provenance really difficult, ideally there would be versions on ARBA IDs, and versions on pipeline runs. Two asides, NOT discussed here - from an evoutionary parsimony perspective, the rule is bonkers (even though it happens to give the right answer here) - the treegrafter on the same gene is likely wrong (#6642)
title: ARBA2GO issue: ARBA rules are misfiring (pipeline error)

author: Antonialock
body: Hi Chris, We have had an issue since the last release where QuickGO is displaying a different dataset from the website. I am told that this will be corrected in the next release (on Wednesday). We now have 8k bacterial entries annotated by ARBA00086692 so I assume something has changed in the underlying data, it will be easier to check on Wednesday. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/annotations?withFrom=ARBA00086692&taxonId=2&taxonUsage=descendants I see a different issue here however: GO:0031956 medium-chain fatty acid-CoA ligase activity, the definition says "medium-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing 6 to 12 carbons" In 2024 the obsolete GO:0047760 butyrate-CoA ligase activity was replaced by GO:0031956 (medium chain), but butyrate is short chain according to GO (it's medium chain according to EC - EC uses a different definition, medium chain "Acts on fatty acids from C4 to C11" https://enzyme.expasy.org/EC/6.2.1.2 ) This means that for example CCL4_HUMLU M4IQQ5 (annotated by the ARBA AND has EXP evidence) is annotated to "medium chain...." but it should be annotated to "short chain" (I'll fix that now) I asked Claude to check if it could find more errors like this, and it found 9 Effect on Swiss-Prot. I checked the history of the 58 reviewed entries that have a primary GO:0031956 annotation (IDA, EXP, ISS or TAS). 21 had a manual GO:0047760 annotation in 2024_03 and the same evidence on GO:0031956 from 2024_05. For M4IQQ5 the move happened between versions v26 and v27. Of those 21: 11 are correct: the enzyme also uses C6+ substrates (ACSM1/2A/3, hop CCL2 and CCL3, Arabidopsis AAE11). 1 cannot be assessed: F1MPP7 (AgBase) has no substrate data. 9 are now wrong: they assert medium-chain activity for enzymes with only C2–C5 substrates. UniProt assigned all nine. Two of them are the wrong training positives behind ARBA00086692: A4YDT1 (the whole-family set) and M4IQQ5 (the fabids set). So the obsoletion is an upstream cause of the over-propagation we discussed. A4YDT1 already had an IEA GO:0031956 from the 2020 EC cross-reference; the migration turned the same mix-up into an experimental annotation. I did not check annotations inferred from these entries by orthology or phylogeny (ISO, IBA), which would spread the error further, for example to ACSS3 orthologues. Fixes Swiss-Prot: change GO:0031956 to GO:0031955 on the nine entries, keeping the evidence and reference. On A4YDT1, A4YDR9 and Q8VZF1, also replace the generic “a medium-chain fatty acid” reaction (RHEA:48340 / EC 6.2.1.2) with explicit reactions, such as butanoate (RHEA:46172) and pentanoate (RHEA:46168). Otherwise the Rhea and EC mappings will regenerate GO:0031956 as IEA. GO ontology: change the GO:0047760 obsoletion to “consider GO:0031955, GO:0031956” (or replaced_by GO:0120515). Move the EC:6.2.1.2 cross-reference from GO:0031956 to GO:0120515. Annotations that have already moved will not revert by themselves.

author: cmungall
body:
It looks like https://www.uniprot.org/arba/ARBA00086692 has gained an OR clause, which makes it consistent with QuickGO / EBI GOA downloads. This was the main issue. It would be great to have more versioning on the rules and for the main Uniprot entry to be more consistent with QuickGO but these are separate issues.

There are different biological issues as you point out, but this is common across many rules, I'll make separate reports for these, for now the main sync issue seems fixed.

author: Antonialock
body: Thanks Chris. I have been told that this sync issue between uniprot website and GOA was a one off and shouldn't happen again (fingers crossed)
